claim: for the sealed, immutable historical role a direct-ordinal (dense) inode-id spine answers identical lookups/ranges/readdir, is more compact, and cannot regress publication or mutation because the live writer spine stays the persistent treap

decision.rule: integrate only where it wins and cannot regress publication or mutation: the sealed layout must be more compact and not slower on the point lookup, and the live spine must remain the treap

design.note: files are created directly under the root so the build is linear; the inode-id spine measured is independent of the directory shape

note: Single run, single host. Absolute nanoseconds are host/build dependent; the *shape* (a direct-ordinal array vs a pointer-heavy treap) and the spine-bytes ratio are the point. `inode_spine_bytes` is a structural lower bound (node/entry capacities, no allocator slop, no inode payloads, which are shared in both layouts). `seal_rebuild_ns` is the one-time cost of building the dense array from the treap, paid only when an accelerator is decoded. The live column records the writer spine's layout and publication cost: it is the treap, so mutation and publication are the pre-existing Phase-27 behaviour.

scales.equivalence: identical lookups, ordered id enumeration, readdir, dentry lookup, parent_of, is_live_dir, latest_offset, canonical digest, and structural equality (asserted)

live.note: the live writer spine is the treap; this integration adds no code to `from_log`/`apply_record`/commit, so live mutation and publication are unchanged by construction
